  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS
Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social distancing measures currently
in effect, and pursuant to Assembly Bill 361, please note that members of the public will be
allowed only to observe and address the City Council Meeting of October 19, 2021, at 2:00
P.M. (Or 1:00 P.M. if Closed Session) by telephone, video and other electronic means, as
follows:

  1. Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
  electronically for consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority
  (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary
  at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk
  at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative
  Body prior to consideration of the agenda, City Clerk staff will check and print emails
  prior to arriving in the Council Chambers. In the body of the email, please identify the
  agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and
  agenda item. Comments received will be made part of the official public record of the
  meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  2. Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the
Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and
regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any person who requires a disability-related

minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  October 19, 2021

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
October 19, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:02 p.m.

The Acting City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and
  Faulk; and
  Absent: None.

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Angela Allen  Acting City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:03 p.m. for Closed Session Item
No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/ Finance
Authority Secretary/Parking Authority Secretary/ Joint Powers Authority Secretary
announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/ Parking Authority
  Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts, Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members/ Parking Authority Members/ Joint Powers Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent: None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint
Powers Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Assistant City Manager/CFO
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance Authority,
Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.
   October 19, 2021

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/ Parking Authority
  Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons
  present who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing
  Authority/Finance Authority/ Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority on any item on
  the Agendas.
  Ronda Mayfair spoke concerning a matter not on the Agenda, and was advised to call
  back towards the end of the meeting to address her concerns.

  142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  October 14, 2021, in the amount of $5,124,139.17, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Council Members/ Successor Agency Members/ Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/ Successor Agency Chairman /
  Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that the Minutes for the Council Meetings held on August 17, 2021,
  August 24, 2021, August 24, 2021 (Special), September 14, 2021, and September 21,
  2021, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 22-013 APPROVED -
  CROSSTOWN ELECTRICAL & DATA, INC. Staff report dated October 19, 2021,
  was presented recommending award of a contract and approval of an agreement with
  Crosstown Electrical & Data, Inc., to provide construction services of facilities for the
  Inglewood Traffic Management Center Project, per Bid No. RFB-0135.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement No. 22-013 in
  the total amount of $3,298,570 (includes a ten percent 10% contingency in the amount of
  $299,870). The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  183  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – JOES’ SWEEPING, INC. DBA NATIONWIDE
  ENVIRONMENTAL  SERVICES  (NATIONWIDE);  ACCOUNTING
  ADJUSTMENT APPROVED – JULY 2021 INVOICE PAID ON SEPTEMBER 10,
  2021. Staff report dated October 19, 2021, was presented recommending authorization to
  pay invoices submitted by Joes’ Sweeping, Inc. dba Nationwide Environmental Services
  (Nationwide) for street sweeping services rendered from March 2021 through June 2021.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve payment in the total amount of $192,
  375.60; and 2) Approve an accounting adjustment for the July 2021 invoice paid on
  September 10, 2021. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
   October 19, 2021

126  GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION SELECTED – NOVEMBER 8, 2022; CITY
  CLERK DIRECTED TO ENSUE WITH THE NECESSARY PROCEDURES TO
  CALL FOR A GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION. Staff report dated October 19,
  2021, was presented recommending the selection of November 8, 2022, as the date for
  the City’s next General Municipal Election to give the City time to conduct public
  hearings required for the redistricting process, in accordance with the FAIR MAPS Act.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Select November 8, 2022, as the date for the next
  General Municipal Election; and 2) Direct the City Clerk to ensue with the necessary
  procedures to call for a General Municipal Election to be held on the selected date. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 301  ORDINANCE NO. 22-01 ADOPTED – APPROVAL OF ZONING CODE
  AMENDMENT 2021-001 (ZCA-2021-001) TO AMEND CHAPTER 12
  (PLANNING AND ZONING) OF THE MUNICIPAL CODE TO MODIFY
  REGULATIONS FOR SMOKE SHOPS, CITYWIDE. Staff report dated October 19,
  2021, was presented recommending adoption of Ordinance No. 22-01, approving Zoning
  Code Amendment 2021-001 (ZCA-2021-001) to amend Chapter 12 (Planning and
  Zoning) of the Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC) to modify Regulations for Smoke
  Shops, Citywide.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that further
  reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Mayor Butts
  that Ordinance No. 22-01 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, TO APPROVE ZONING CODE
  AMENDMENT 2021-001 (ZCA-2021-001) TO AMEND CHAPTER 12
  (PLANNING AND ZONING) OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL
  CODE TO MODIFY REGULATIONS FOR SMOKE SHOPS

  which was introduced at the meeting held October 12, 2021, be adopted. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132.6  CLOSED SESSION – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION WITH LEGAL COUNSEL
  AND (ONE POTENTIAL CASE). Closed Session – Confidential – Attorney/Client
  Privileged; City Council Conference with Legal Counsel regarding anticipated litigation
  pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2); (One Potential Case).

  Direction given; No action taken.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, reported she attended the
  Ribbon Cutting Ceremony for the Judith & Thomas Beckmen YOLA Center, and how
  exciting it was to hear such melodic sounds exuding from the students’ instruments. In
  addition, she wished Council Member Morales a happy birthday.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Ronda Mayfair commented that there is a hole in the street on Century and Hardy caused
  by a line break. She also requested to know when it would be repaired.

  3
 October 19, 2021

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned, at the hour of 2:16 p.m.

  Approved this 26th day of October, 2021.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
